meta: A Christian look at the false belief that good Christians don’t have problems, with Scripture, questions, and homework for replacing it with the truth.
origins: Growing up in a family that hid its problems to look good at church. Hearing testimonies that ended with “and now everything is wonderful.” Being told that troubles mean you are out of God’s will. Feeling ashamed to admit struggles to other believers. A church culture that rewarded looking “fine.”
teaches: Jesus said plainly, “In the world you will have tribulation.” Scripture tells us not to be surprised by fiery trials, as though something strange were happening. Many are the afflictions of the righteous, but the LORD delivers them. Trials are part of the Christian life and can produce perseverance and maturity. Good Christians have problems; what makes them different is where they take their problems.
self_statements: If I were a better Christian, I wouldn’t have these problems.
I have to look like I have it all together.
Other Christians don’t struggle like I do.
My problems prove I’m failing God.
I can’t tell anyone at church what’s really going on.
errors: Comparing your real life to other people’s public image.
Seeing every problem as proof of personal failure.
Overlooking the many struggles of faithful people in Scripture.
questions: What did Jesus promise about trouble in this world?
Did the people of faith in the Bible have problems?
Am I comparing my inside to other people’s outside?
Who taught me to hide my problems?
What does James say trials can produce?
What would happen if I were honest with one safe person?
Is the goal a problem-free life or a faithful one?
truth: Good Christians have problems. Jesus said I would have trouble in this world, and He has overcome it. My problems do not prove I am failing God. Trials can grow perseverance and maturity in me. I can be honest about my struggles and bring them to God and to His people.
hw_questions: What did Jesus promise about trouble?

log: Each day, write one real struggle and one way God helped me with it.
name_example: Many are the afflictions of Sarah, but the LORD delivers her from them all.
actions: Tell one safe Christian about a real struggle
this week, and notice how they respond.
Read about one Bible hero’s problems,
such as David, Elijah, or Paul, and write what they faced.
“What’s the hardest thing you’ve gone through as a Christian?”
Join or visit a small group
where people share honestly and pray for one another.
tracker: One struggle I brought to God
prayer: Lord Jesus, thank You for telling me the truth: in this world I will have trouble, but You have overcome the world. Help me reject the lie that good Christians don’t have problems. Give me courage to be honest, and grow perseverance and faith in me through my trials. In Your name, Amen.
